abstract: DNA methylation is an important epigenetic mechanism regulating gene expression, and its maintenance depends on cellular methyl group metabolism. Adenosylhomocysteinase (AHCY) is a key enzyme in the methionine cycle that hydrolyzes S-adenosylhomocysteine (SAH), thereby preventing its accumulation and inhibition of methyltransferase activity. Although AHCY has been implicated in cancer cell proliferation and transcriptional regulation, the effects of its inhibition on genome-wide DNA methylation and their relationship to gene expression remain poorly understood in colorectal cancer (CRC). Here, we investigated the consequences of pharmacological AHCY inhibition in GP5d colorectal cancer cells by integrating metabolomic profiling, nanopore sequencing-based DNA methylation analysis and RNA sequencing. AHCY inhibition resulted in SAH accumulation, widespread DNA hypomethylation and reduced cell proliferation, accompanied by changes in purine metabolism and gene expression. Despite the overall loss of DNA methylation, localized hypermethylation was also observed, particularly at CpG-rich regulatory regions. Transcriptomic analysis revealed changes in proliferation-associated and cell cycle checkpoint pathways, including strong upregulation of the cell cycle regulator CDKN1A. Importantly, promoter hypomethylation was significantly enriched among upregulated genes, including genes involved in cell cycle regulation, whereas gene body hypomethylation showed no comparable association with differential gene expression. Together, these findings demonstrate that AHCY inhibition induces extensive metabolic, epigenetic and transcriptional changes in CRC cells and suggest that promoter hypomethylation may contribute to the transcriptional responses associated with reduced cell proliferation.
